tore pr-review skill

Skills aren't reliably auto-invoked in claude-code-action automation mode
(action #1003), so inject the skill as a system prompt:
- Fetch SKILL.md from the trusted openmrs-module-querystore repo into a
  temp path outside the PR checkout (a malicious PR can't substitute it),
  failing loudly if missing/unexpected.
- Pass it via --append-system-prompt-file; replace the hand-written prompt
  with a skill invocation over this PR; drop the forced header (it fights
  the skill's anti-bot-fingerprint rules; the bot identity discloses it).
- Give the step GH_TOKEN so the skill's gh-based posting is authenticated.
- Raise --max-turns to 40 and timeout to 30m for the skill's deeper flow.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Harden skill integration: full history for the skill; hoist SKILL_URL

- fetch-depth: 0 — the skill's local-git verification (merge-base, diff
  against base, drift checks) can't run on a shallow single-ref checkout.
- Hoist SKILL_URL to the top-level env next to the other tunables, so
  pinning the methodology to a commit SHA is a one-line change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Forbid executing untrusted PR code during review

Add a prompt constraint (overriding the skill) that bars running mvn,
gradle, npm, builds, or any script/binary from the PR tree; verification
is read-only (git diff/grep, gh pr diff, gh api). Build-only checks are
reported as questions per the skill's own can't-run-the-experiment rule.
Closes the arbitrary-code-execution vector where building an untrusted PR
could exfiltrate the review secrets. Update the stale timeout comment.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Clarify the no-exec constraint so it doesn't block posting

Scope the ban explicitly to the PR's own build/tests/scripts, and state
that Claude's own read-only tooling is expected: git, gh, curl for
upstream refs, and python to assemble the review payload it posts. Avoids
a silent failure where an over-broad reading of 'never execute any code'
stops the review from being posted (indistinguishable from a clean PR).

rows.excerpt:
ode> as the end [PR #4358](pgjdbc/pgjdbc#4358)
  • fix: LargeObjectManager operations now work inside an active XA transaction. Since 42.7.13 an XA branch keeps the caller's autoCommit=true, and the guard rejected large objects as if the connection were idle. It now checks the server transaction state (getTransactionState()) instead of autoCommit, so a genuine auto-commit connection with no open transaction is still refused [Issue #4309](pgjdbc/pgjdbc#4309) [PR #4310](pgjdbc/pgjdbc#4310)
  • fix: batch update counts are no longer secured as committed inside an XA transaction. BatchResultHandler treated per-statement progress as durable whenever autoCommit=true, but an XA branch keeps autoCommit=true while the transaction is open, so a batch that flushed mid-way and then failed could report rolled-back statements as succeeded. Progress is now secured only when no server transaction is open [Issue #4309](pgjdbc/pgjdbc#4309) [PR #4311](pgjdbc/pgjdbc#4311)

    • Changed

    • fix: backend message lengths are checked before anything is sized from them. Each length is checked against the message layout and a limit for its type, the lengths inside DataRow and FunctionCallResponse are checked against the message, and the NegotiateProtocolVersion option count is bounded. A hostile or out of sync backend could previously force an allocation of up to two gigabytes with a five byte header [Issue #4015](pgjdbc/pgjdbc#4015)
